# Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction

Also called: Animatable Gaussian Avatars, Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting for Humans

## Overview
Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction refers to a family of methods that reconstruct animatable, photorealistic 3D human or head avatars by representing them as collections of 3D Gaussians [S1, unofficial]. Unlike static scene reconstruction, these methods must handle non-rigid deformation, ensuring that the Gaussian primitives move and deform consistently with the underlying subject's pose and expression [S1, unofficial]. The family is distinguished from static [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) [946-gaussian-splatting.md] by its integration of parametric body models (e.g., SMPL, FLAME) or deformation fields to constrain and drive the Gaussian positions, and from [neural radiance field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) avatars by its explicit, rasterizable representation that enables real-time rendering speeds [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on differentiable rendering to compute gradients from the rendered image to the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) and/or network weights [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, unofficial]. The rendering process remains differentiable with respect to the scene representation [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, unofficial]. Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].

A core principle is the anchoring of Gaussians to a geometric prior. Most methods initialize Gaussians on the surface of a parametric mesh (e.g., SMPL for full body, FLAME for heads) in a canonical rest pose [S1, 1477-gaussian-avatars.md, 1482-relightable-gaussian-codec-avatars.md, unofficial]. During training, these Gaussians are deformed to match the target pose using rigid transformations (e.g., Linear Blend Skinning) and/or non-rigid deformation fields [S1, 8385-smpl-based-rigid-non-rigid-deformation.md, unofficial]. This ensures that the avatar can be animated to novel poses while maintaining structural integrity [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Splatting](946-gaussian-splatting.md)
The foundational static rendering method. Not an avatar method itself, but the rendering engine used by all avatar variants.

### [GaussianShader](1470-gaussianshader.md)
Enriches Gaussians with physical material parameters (diffusiveness, specularity, roughness, normals) to enable specular and reflective rendering. Distinguished by explicit material properties rather than view-dependent color alone.

### [SpotlessSplats](1476-spotlesssplats.md)
Enhances robustness against transient distractors (e.g., moving people, lighting changes) in casual video captures by detecting outliers in a pre-trained feature space. Builds on Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction by adding feature-based outlier detection.

### [Gaussian Avatars](1477-gaussian-avatars.md)
Reconstructs photorealistic, animatable head avatars by associating 3D Gaussians with FLAME mesh triangles. Distinguished by explicit triangle-to-Gaussian mapping rather than MLP-based position prediction, and focuses on the head/bust region.

### [Relightable Gaussian Codec Avatars](1482-relightable-gaussian-codec-avatars.md)
Creates photorealistic, animatable 3D head avatars that support dynamic relighting under diverse lighting conditions. Builds on Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction by integrating a relightable appearance model with a FLAME-based parametric rig.

### [NoPoSplat](1484-noposplat.md)
A [3D Gaussian Splatting method](#4010-gaussian-kernel-volumetric-primitive.md) for novel view synthesis from sparse or unposed input images. Eliminates dependency on known camera poses by establishing a canonical coordinate system anchored to a single input view and using intrinsics token embeddings.

### [SMPL-based rigid/non-rigid deformation](8385-smpl-based-rigid-non-rigid-deformation.md)
Reconstructs animatable 3D human avatars by anchoring Gaussians to SMPL/SMPL-X models. Solves generalization to novel poses by combining rigid skeletal transformations with pose-conditioned non-rigid deformation fields.

### Codec Avatar 3D
- [S1, unofficial] A production-grade GS-based head model for volumetric telepresence by Meta.

### OmniRe
- [S1, unofficial] A holistic scene reconstruction method including humans, vehicles, and static background.

### SplatArmor
- [S2] Leverage two different MLPs to predict large motions built upon the SMPL and canonical space.
- [S2] Allow pose-dependent effects by the proposed SE(3) fields.

## Background
The field emerged from the success of 3D Gaussian Splatting [946-gaussian-splatting.md] for static scene rendering [S1, unofficial]. Early attempts to animate Gaussians relied on neural deformation fields or tetrahedral cages [S2]. The introduction of parametric model integration, such as [Gaussian Avatars](#1477-gaussian-avatars.md) using FLAME [S1, 1477-gaussian-avatars.md, unofficial] and SMPL-based methods [S1, 8385-smpl-based-rigid-non-rigid-deformation.md, unofficial], provided a robust geometric prior for non-rigid deformation. Recent developments include relightable avatars [S2, 1482-relightable-gaussian-codec-avatars.md] and robust training against distractors [S1, 1476-spotlesssplats.md, unofficial]. Production-grade implementations like Meta's Codec Avatar 3D [S1, unofficial] and holistic scene reconstruction methods like OmniRe [S1, unofficial] indicate industry adoption for telepresence and simulation [S1, unofficial].
